0e8729cb7b617ee4.title: Hwaljjak Tablet
0e8729cb7b617ee4.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite (poor appetite), overeating, food stagnation, promotion of digestion, upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion, nausea, and vomiting.
0e8729cb7b617ee4.usage:
Those aged 15 and over take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Allow at least 4 hours between doses.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
0e8729cb7b617ee4.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: children aged 7 or under, patients hypersensitive to soybean oil or with a history of allergic reactions to it, or patients hypersensitive to soybeans or peanuts.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, or are pregnant or possibly pregnant.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Patients with a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or patients requiring careful administration of lipid emulsions, should take this medicine with caution.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

1caa441848f10fd1.title: Aipia Soft Capsule
1caa441848f10fd1.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to relieve dryness of the eyes, for poor development of bone, for the prevention of night blindness and rickets, and to supply vitamins A and D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age.
1caa441848f10fd1.usage:
Adults aged 15 and over take 2 capsules once a day; those aged 7 to under 15 take 1 capsule once a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
1caa441848f10fd1.caution:
Warning: Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations. Do not take this medicine if you are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or possibly pregnant.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: if skin itching, nausea, or vomiting occurs after taking, if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, or patients hypersensitive to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or are possibly pregnant.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a pharmacist when taking together with intravenous lipid preparations.

If diarrhea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Relief of dryness of the eyes; prevention of night blindness and rickets; supply of vitamins A and D…
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Relief of dryness of the eyes; poor development of bone; prevention of night blindness and rickets; supply of vitamins A and D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age

26025df241557f80.title: Dicamax 1000 Tablet
26025df241557f80.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to supply calcium for calcium deficiency and other calcium needs.
26025df241557f80.usage:
Adults and those aged 8 and over take 1 tablet once a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
26025df241557f80.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, or patients with hypercalcemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones, or severe renal failure, or infants under 12 months of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist in the case of children who get plenty of sunlight and eat a normal diet, if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, or hypoproteinemia, or have had kidney stones.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when using together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supply of vitamin D; prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; supply of calcium…
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Supply of vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age; prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; supply of calcium for calcium deficiency and other calcium needs

262be157b0e4825d.title: Ganejin Tablet
262be157b0e4825d.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment for chronic hepatitis and toxic liver disease.
262be157b0e4825d.usage:
Adults take 1 tablet at a time, 2 to 3 times a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
262be157b0e4825d.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are deficient in folic acid.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

This medicine may turn the urine yellow in various urine tests, affecting clinical test values.

Do not take together with levodopa.

If you experience itching, skin rash, redness (flushing), constipation, nausea, or upper abdominal discomfort, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Adjunctive treatment for chronic hepatitis and toxic liver disease
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Adjunctive treatment for chronic hepatitis and toxic liver disease

263b17547f3e5e24.title: Baegana Tablet
263b17547f3e5e24.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to improve excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching, and indigestion associated with peptic ulcer.
263b17547f3e5e24.usage:
Adults take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times a day between meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
263b17547f3e5e24.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients on dialysis, patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption, women who are pregnant or possibly pregnant, women who are breastfeeding, or children (under 15 years of age).

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have experienced allergic reactions (rash, redness, itching, etc.), have kidney impairment, liver impairment, or low phosphate levels, have high blood pressure or are elderly, have a heart or kidney disorder, or have edema (swelling).

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

Do not take together with gastrointestinal analgesics or antispasmodics. Take with caution when using together with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), as pseudoaldosteronism or hypokalemia may make myopathy (muscle disease) more likely.

If you experience decreased urine output, swelling of the face or hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, rising blood pressure, headache, myopathy (muscle disease), allergic reactions (rash, itching, etc.), or rarely palpitations, drowsiness, dizziness, fatigue, constipation, dry mouth, pounding heartbeat, or elevated GOT and GPT levels, or if symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Improvement of excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, and indigestion associated with peptic ulcer…
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Improvement of excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching, and indigestion associated with peptic ulcer

3f21c651205a3b2d.title: Dicabon 300 Tablet
3f21c651205a3b2d.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to supply calcium for calcium deficiency and other calcium needs.
3f21c651205a3b2d.usage:
Adults and those aged 8 and over take 1 tablet once a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
3f21c651205a3b2d.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, or patients with hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones, severe renal failure, or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist in the case of infants under 1 year of age or children who get plenty of sunlight and eat a normal diet, if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, or hypoproteinemia, have had kidney stones, or are taking cardiac glycosides.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when taking together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.Main symptoms: Supply of vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age; prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; supply of calcium for calcium deficiency and other calcium needs

3fc4b2d180d678c4.title: Megabicom Tablet
3fc4b2d180d678c4.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and lowered physical strength during or after illness, to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness), for beriberi and eye fatigue, and to relieve angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (sores in the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema, and dermatitis.
3fc4b2d180d678c4.usage:
Adults and those aged 8 and over take 1 tablet once a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
3fc4b2d180d678c4.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, infants under 3 months of age, or patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist in the case of infants under 1 year of age, or if you have hyperoxaluria, are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have gout or kidney stones, or are deficient in folic acid.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of blood sugar in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values.

Do not take together with levodopa.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or loose stools, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

46ffa6d03d0eb6dc.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching, indigestion, loss of appetite (poor appetite), overeating, promotion of digestion, and stomach bloating caused by indigestion.

4840d3b5304687cc.title: Conti 600 Tablet
4840d3b5304687cc.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, and B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and lowered physical strength during or after illness, to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness), and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
4840d3b5304687cc.usage:
Children aged 12 and over and adults take 1 tablet once a day after meals.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, infants under 3 months of age, or patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you are deficient in folic acid.

4cd5aacc94a0af56.title: Twice Plus Soft Capsule
4cd5aacc94a0af56.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E and B1 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, and in old age, to relieve peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet, to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness), for beriberi and eye fatigue, and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
4cd5aacc94a0af56.usage:
Adults and those aged 12 and over take 1 capsule at a time, twice a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
4cd5aacc94a0af56.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts, infants under 12 months of age, or patients with severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis, cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, hypoproteinemia, a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, require careful administration of lipid emulsions, are at particular risk from fat overload, or have a predisposition to thrombosis (blood vessel blockage).

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, decreased central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, or if menstruation starts earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier, or bleeding lasts longer, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
